newsitem.title: USA: Duff sets Uruguay obligations at triple-B-minus.
newsitem.headline: Duff sets Uruguay obligations at triple-B-minus.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Tuesday it assigned a triple-B-minus rating to the foreign currency obligations of Uruguay.
Duff said the investment grade rating reflects Uruguay's strong external debt ratios, favorable social indicators, stable political environment and ongoing structural reforms.
The rating is constrained, it added, by the country's traditionally high, volatile and heavily indexed inflation rate, and its economic dependence on Argentina and Brazil.
However, economic policy has curbed inflation in Uruguay, from 130 precent in 1990 to 24 percent in 1996. A "reasonable target" of 15 percent for 1997 was set recently, Duff added.
